title: ROOT: Command a satellite over an unauthenticated telecommand link (Space Odyssey class)
text: Decomposition of the missing-telecommand-authentication finding reported for real in-orbit satellites. Objective: from a rogue uplink, issue a telecommand the spacecraft accepts because the link has no cryptographic authentication, then change an on-board value to degrade the mission. Targets are emulated flight software on a bench.
source: Willbold et al., Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites, IEEE S&P 2023; SPARTA.

title: Characterize the commanding protocol
text: Sub-step. Enumerate the telecommand frame format and command dictionary of the target bus. Deterministic check: reconstructed TC frame that the emulated receiver parses.
source: Willbold et al., Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites, IEEE S&P 2023; SPARTA.

title: Stand up a rogue uplink
text: Sub-step. Transmit from an external station the spacecraft cannot distinguish from the real operator. Deterministic check: emulated receiver accepts frames from the rogue station.
source: Willbold et al., Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites, IEEE S&P 2023; SPARTA.

title: Issue an unauthenticated telecommand
text: Sub-step. Send a command that is executed because no authentication is enforced on the link. Deterministic check: on-board value changes to the commanded setting on the bench.
source: Willbold et al., Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites, IEEE S&P 2023; SPARTA.

title: Degrade the mission
text: Sub-step. Use the accepted command to reduce a mission function, such as mispointing an antenna. Deterministic check: measured degradation of the emulated function versus baseline.
source: Willbold et al., Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites, IEEE S&P 2023; SPARTA.

title: ROOT: Take control of an on-board experiment environment (OPS-SAT authorized exercise)
text: Decomposition of an authorized ethical-hacking exercise against a flying experimental testbed. Objective: from code running inside the hosted experiment slot, reach system interfaces and manipulate a payload, then persist. Conducted under an explicit consent-to-test agreement.
source: Thales / ESA OPS-SAT ethical-hacking demonstration, CYSAT 2023; ESA; SPARTA.

title: Execute code in the hosted experiment
text: Sub-step. Run attacker-supplied code inside the experiment container provided to third parties. Deterministic check: code executes in the experiment sandbox on the emulated bench.
source: Thales / ESA OPS-SAT ethical-hacking demonstration, CYSAT 2023; ESA; SPARTA.

title: Reach system interfaces
text: Sub-step. From the experiment slot, call system APIs to change ADCS or payload parameters. Deterministic check: on-board parameter changes from within the experiment context.
source: Thales / ESA OPS-SAT ethical-hacking demonstration, CYSAT 2023; ESA; SPARTA.

title: Persist in the experiment slot
text: Sub-step. Install a hook that survives an experiment restart. Deterministic check: hook re-executes after a simulated experiment restart.
source: Thales / ESA OPS-SAT ethical-hacking demonstration, CYSAT 2023; ESA; SPARTA.

title: Manipulate a payload function
text: Sub-step. Alter a payload output such as the imager to degrade its product. Deterministic check: payload output deviates from the expected emulated baseline.
source: Thales / ESA OPS-SAT ethical-hacking demonstration, CYSAT 2023; ESA; SPARTA.

title: ROOT: Decrypt satellite phone traffic by exploiting a weak air-interface cipher (GMR-1/GMR-2)
text: Decomposition of the satphone-cipher analysis of the GMR-1 and GMR-2 standards. Objective: from a recorded downlink, exploit the weak stream cipher to recover keystream and reconstruct call content. Confidentiality attack; capture is of an emulated or consented link.
source: Driessen et al., Don't Trust Satellite Phones: A Security Analysis of Two Satphone Standards, IEEE S&P 2012; SPARTA.

title: Identify the air-interface standard
text: Sub-step. Fingerprint the GMR framing and burst structure of the captured signal. Deterministic check: demodulated bursts align to the documented GMR frame layout.
source: Driessen et al., Don't Trust Satellite Phones: A Security Analysis of Two Satphone Standards, IEEE S&P 2012; SPARTA.

title: Intercept and demodulate the downlink
text: Sub-step. Capture and demodulate the satphone downlink bursts. Deterministic check: recorded I/Q yields decoded ciphertext bursts.
source: Driessen et al., Don't Trust Satellite Phones: A Security Analysis of Two Satphone Standards, IEEE S&P 2012; SPARTA.

title: Recover keystream and decrypt
text: Sub-step. Exploit the weak stream cipher to recover keystream and reconstruct plaintext. Deterministic check: decrypted frame matches a known-plaintext control message.
source: Driessen et al., Don't Trust Satellite Phones: A Security Analysis of Two Satphone Standards, IEEE S&P 2012; SPARTA.

title: ROOT: Recover message content from an unencrypted satellite link (Iridium class)
text: Decomposition of open-source Iridium decoding of an unencrypted link. Objective: capture the L-band downlink and reassemble plaintext messages that travel without link-layer encryption. Passive confidentiality attack against an emulated or consented feed.
source: gr-iridium / iridium-toolkit (muccc; Sec and Schneider); 'Iridium Update', 32C3, 2015; SPARTA.

title: Identify the link framing
text: Sub-step. Characterize the Iridium L-band framing and channel plan. Deterministic check: demodulated frames align to the documented Iridium structure.
source: gr-iridium / iridium-toolkit (muccc; Sec and Schneider); 'Iridium Update', 32C3, 2015; SPARTA.

title: Capture and demodulate the downlink
text: Sub-step. Record the L-band downlink with an SDR and demodulate frames. Deterministic check: SDR capture yields decoded link-layer frames.
source: gr-iridium / iridium-toolkit (muccc; Sec and Schneider); 'Iridium Update', 32C3, 2015; SPARTA.

title: Reassemble plaintext messages
text: Sub-step. Reassemble message content that is sent without link-layer encryption. Deterministic check: reconstructed message matches an emulated reference transmission.
source: gr-iridium / iridium-toolkit (muccc; Sec and Schneider); 'Iridium Update', 32C3, 2015; SPARTA.

title: ROOT: Re-execute a privileged action by replaying a captured telecommand (no anti-replay)
text: Decomposition of a replay against a telecommand link that lacks anti-replay protection (for example CCSDS without SDLS). Objective: capture an authentic telecommand and retransmit it within the acceptance window so the action executes again. Targets are emulated.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Characterize the acceptance window
text: Sub-step. Determine the telecommand frame format and the counters or timetags that gate acceptance. Deterministic check: documented acceptance conditions for a valid TC frame.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Capture an authentic telecommand
text: Sub-step. Record a legitimate telecommand frame on the uplink. Deterministic check: stored TC frame that the emulated receiver validates.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Replay the captured frame
text: Sub-step. Retransmit the captured frame within the acceptance window because no anti-replay is enforced. Deterministic check: emulated receiver accepts the replayed frame a second time.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Re-apply the on-board state change
text: Sub-step. The replayed command re-applies its state change on the target. Deterministic check: on-board value returns to the replayed setting.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: ROOT: Extract and patch firmware through an enabled debug interface (development-time exposure)
text: Decomposition of a hardware debug exposure caught during development. Objective: use a debug interface left enabled on the flight hardware to read firmware and load a modified image, then persist. Shift-left, bench-only against development hardware.
source: SPARTA; common enabled-debug-interface exposure on flight hardware.

title: Locate the enabled debug interface
text: Sub-step. Identify exposed JTAG or SWD test points and the target microcontroller. Deterministic check: debug probe halts the core over the exposed interface.
source: SPARTA; common enabled-debug-interface exposure on flight hardware.

title: Load modified firmware
text: Sub-step. Patch the secure-boot check or write a modified image through the debug port. Deterministic check: modified image runs past the boot integrity check on the bench.
source: SPARTA; common enabled-debug-interface exposure on flight hardware.

title: Persist the modified image
text: Sub-step. Write the modified image so it survives a power cycle. Deterministic check: modified image re-runs after a bench reset.
source: SPARTA; common enabled-debug-interface exposure on flight hardware.

title: ROOT: Verify the serial console is not an unauthenticated foothold on the flight build
text: Development-time bench check. Objective: connect to the board's UART, determine whether it exposes an unauthenticated shell, a bootloader interrupt, or secret-leaking logs, and confirm the flight build disables or authenticates the console. Bench-only against development hardware.
source: SPARTA; serial-console exposure in embedded flight software (shift-left check).

title: Identify the UART interface
text: Sub-step. Locate the UART test points and determine the baud rate and framing on the dev board. Deterministic check: readable console banner captured on the serial line.
source: SPARTA; serial-console exposure in embedded flight software (shift-left check).

title: Test for an unauthenticated console
text: Sub-step. Interact with the console to check whether it accepts commands without authentication. Deterministic check: flight build requires authentication or the console is absent, not an open shell.
source: SPARTA; serial-console exposure in embedded flight software (shift-left check).

title: Test for a bootloader interrupt
text: Sub-step. Attempt to interrupt the bootloader over the console to reach a lower-level prompt. Deterministic check: flight build ignores the interrupt rather than dropping to a bootloader prompt.
source: SPARTA; serial-console exposure in embedded flight software (shift-left check).

title: Check for secret leakage in console output
text: Sub-step. Review console and log output for keys, credentials, or memory addresses. Deterministic check: no sensitive material appears in the flight-build console output.
source: SPARTA; serial-console exposure in embedded flight software (shift-left check).

title: ROOT: Verify the RF link enforces authentication, anti-replay, and confidentiality at the bench
text: Development-time bench check. Objective: attach an SDR to the dev flatsat, send a telecommand and receive telemetry, and verify the link authenticates commands, rejects replays, and does not expose sensitive telemetry in plaintext. Emulated flatsat, no on-orbit action.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Establish the SDR link
text: Sub-step. Configure the SDR to the link frequency and framing and exchange frames with the flatsat. Deterministic check: SDR closes the link and a valid telecommand is acknowledged.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Verify command authentication
text: Sub-step. Send a telecommand without valid authentication from the SDR. Deterministic check: flatsat rejects the unauthenticated command in the flight build.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Verify anti-replay
text: Sub-step. Capture a valid telecommand and retransmit it to the flatsat. Deterministic check: flatsat rejects the replayed frame with anti-replay enforced.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: Verify downlink confidentiality
text: Sub-step. Receive and demodulate the telemetry downlink and inspect it for plaintext sensitive fields. Deterministic check: sensitive telemetry fields are encrypted, not readable in the capture.
source: CCSDS 355.0-B Space Data Link Security; SPARTA.

title: ROOT: Verify internal bus registers and tables are not writable without authorization
text: Development-time bench check. Objective: probe an internal bus (I2C, CAN, MIL-STD-1553, or SpaceWire) on the dev harness and verify that sensitive registers, parameter tables, and mode controls cannot be modified without authorization. Bench-only against development hardware.
source: SPARTA; internal-bus authorization checks (shift-left).

title: Map the internal bus
text: Sub-step. Enumerate bus devices and the register and table map on the dev harness. Deterministic check: device map matches the documented bus topology.
source: SPARTA; internal-bus authorization checks (shift-left).

title: Attempt an unauthorized register write
text: Sub-step. Write to a sensitive register or parameter table over the bus without authorization. Deterministic check: write is rejected or gated by authorization in the flight build.
source: SPARTA; internal-bus authorization checks (shift-left).

title: Attempt to disable fault management over the bus
text: Sub-step. Try to turn off an FDIR monitor through a bus command. Deterministic check: FDIR controls resist unauthorized change over the bus.
source: SPARTA; internal-bus authorization checks (shift-left).

title: ROOT: Command a spacecraft through reduced protections after forcing safe mode
text: Decomposition of safe-mode abuse. Objective: trip a monitored limit to drive the vehicle into safe mode, then issue commands accepted under the relaxed authentication that some safe modes use. Targets are emulated flight software.
source: SPARTA IA-0010; ECSS FDIR/safe-mode practice.

title: Learn the safe-mode triggers
text: Sub-step. Determine which monitored limits enter safe mode and the reduced command set it exposes. Deterministic check: documented safe-mode entry condition and command set.
source: SPARTA IA-0010; ECSS FDIR/safe-mode practice.

title: Force entry into safe mode
text: Sub-step. Change a monitored on-board value to trip a limit and drive the vehicle to safe mode. Deterministic check: emulated FDIR transitions the vehicle into safe mode.
source: SPARTA IA-0010; ECSS FDIR/safe-mode practice.

title: Command under relaxed protections
text: Sub-step. Issue commands accepted under safe mode's reduced authentication. Deterministic check: command accepted in safe mode that baseline mode would reject.
source: SPARTA IA-0010; ECSS FDIR/safe-mode practice.
